rules.instruction: When the description says the participant places an order for materials with one or more outside providers, and the activity is performed by the participant itself, with no message being the unit of work: Model the placing of the order as a user task named from the description's wording, not as a send task. Use a send task only when the description's modeled unit is the sending of a message itself. Keep the order task in the same branch as its preceding step and connect the concurrent work described as happening meanwhile in separate branches, as the parallel-split guidelines already require.
rules.situation: the description says the participant places an order for materials with one or more outside providers, and the activity is performed by the participant itself, with no message being the unit of work

rules.instruction: When the description names an external party, such as another organization, a remote service, or a user-facing system, that exchanges messages with the process while the process runs: Model each such external party as its own pool, not as a lane inside the process's pool. Show the exchanges with it as message flows between the pools: from the process's sending tasks to the external pool, and from the external pool to the process's receiving events or tasks. Do not draw these exchanges as sequence flows, and do not place the external party in a lane of the process pool.
rules.situation: the description says the process sends something to a party outside it and then receives a reply, notice, or delivery back from that party while the process keeps running, and the outside party is described as a distinct participant rather than a step of the process

rules.instruction: When the description states that a party returns an item the requester must rework, and the requester applies further input to it several times, so the rework is repeated: Model the wait for the returned item as an intermediate catch event after the request task. Model each rework round as a task that applies the additional input. After each rework task, place an exclusive decision gateway with one flow back to the request task (for another round sent to the same party) and one flow onward. Do not route the rework straight into the next step, and do not skip the decision that ends the repetition.
rules.situation: the description states that a party returns an item the requester must rework, and the requester applies further input to it several times, so the rework is repeated

rules.instruction: When The description states an activity together with its object and a named recipient or performer (for example, items sent to one or several parties, or work done by a stated party), and the activity is to be modeled as a send, receive or manual task.: Label the task with the verb and object the description uses, and keep the stated recipient or performer in the label. If the description names several recipients or performers for the same activity, keep that whole set in the label, or model one task per recipient when they are handled separately. Do not narrow the set to a single party that the description does not name.
rules.situation: the description says the modeler asks several other parties to carry out a stated piece of work, and the asking is only the way the work gets started, not the work itself

rules.instruction: When the description says an artifact received from another party is refined repeatedly with additional input before the process moves on: Model the repeated refinement as a loop: the refinement activity is followed by an exclusive gateway that tests whether the artifact is sufficient, with one branch returning to the refinement activity and the other continuing to the next step. Model the wait for the returned artifact as an intermediate catch event.
rules.situation: the description says an artifact received from another party is refined repeatedly with additional input before the process moves on

rules.instruction: When the description lists two or more activities that are performed without a stated order and must all be completed before a later step begins: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one outgoing branch per listed activity, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches before the next step. Do not chain the activities in sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway for them.
rules.situation: the description states that one activity is performed while another, separate activity is ongoing, so both run at the same time and their results are needed before the flow continues
